Dynasty Warriors 8XLCE is pretty much the epitome of a Musou game. It is extremely repetitive, because all you do is killing thousands of enemies which have zero chance against you for several hundred hours on end with several dozen characters, over a hundred weapon styles and on quite oftenly repeating maps. And I personally wouldn't have it any other way. The repetitive gameplay aside (and that's what the entire genre is about in the first place) Dynasty Warriors 8 contains so much content that it can be considered the largest Musou game ever developed so far, even before any DLCs are taken into account. I personally wouldn't consider it to be the best game to start to get knowing the Musou genre due to its sheer mountain of content and different game modes though, as it quite possibly could overwhelm new players. The entire menu design, combat and win conditions for maps are all engineered towards players who have completed half a dozen if not more Musou games, so I can imagine playing this without having played Japanese games before or any other genre titles before could simply confuse new players. There is an entry bar to liking the entire genre in the first place though, so I don't consider that design choice to be a bad thing.
Visually DW8XLCE does a good job, the port is solid for the most part, but again, just like most Koei Tecmo games, it's imperative to have a controller at hand as there is no mouse support for the menus and the keyboard layout is dysfunctional at best. In my several hundred hours of playtime I didn't encounter any noteworthy bugs or glitches, framerates were stable. The only downside is controllers having to be mapped manually, but it is only done once and doesn't take longer than 5 minutes if one uses one of the steam guides for the standard console button layout as reference. Just swap A and B and you're gold.
Even although I more than recommend DW8XLCE, it should be made known that this is a niche genre with a very particular fanbase which comes down to that fact that the repetitive gameplay and murdering hundreds of thousands of enemies throughout just a single playthrough of one of the many modes does not agree with everyone, as the enemies have zero to little variety except for enemy captains which in turn use a set of weapon styles which are akin to the ones the player may freely choose from.
Personally I'm a fan of the Warring States period of ancient China and all characters having retained their original Chinese names, but large parts of the Western audience might not be able to make anything of those, let alone keep the names of several dozen player characters and several hundred NPCs apart. Doesn't make it any less fun though.

8.1/10 - Satisfactory single-handed destruction of entire armies.
DW8:XL is an overpowered, weapon-based brawler that allows you to rain hell on waves of armed fighters sent flooding your way. The premise is simple, and there are very few objectives in-game that deviate away from "hit all the guys till there are no more guys", but that is fine and can be quite rewarding. New weapons are available by beating the generals (or unit Commanders) which gives you a wide choice of attack sytles to utilise. EX mode adds a little flavour to this weapon system by giving you character-specific attacks for particular weapons.
The music is the Marmite factor here for me. I always seem to turn it down as it gets a bit much and slightly obnoxious after a while. Bear in-mind that a certain 'level' will cost you half-an-hour, having the same rock BGM on-loop drives you a little mad. While this is not a deal-breaker, it can be annoying, but a least the option is there to reduce it or turn it off.
The FMV's are pretty bad this time around, with entirely wooden and staged performances, it doesnt really convey any real emotions to the audience. Not that this matters entirely, but this is (in comparison) quite an expensive game and with this level of packaging, you expect a little more for your money.
Modes available to play outside the main game really help the replay value, and are very much a positve experience. Ambition mode is probably going to be the one that holds players attention as it allows you to 'build-up' a base as well building upon your chosen character/s.
The real slammer for this game, and the reason why I couldn't find it in myself to give it a 9/10, is controller support. Its terrible. I have a wireless 360, which (in 2017) I had to manually map the buttons, but only after turning the controller on before the game is launched, not after, or it wont be recognised. The wired XBONE controller had less issue, but still there are no button-promts that are XYAB relational. Again, this is an expensive game, and stuff like controller support should be fundemental.
Overall, great game with tonnes of replay value. Excellent vaiety of weaponary and playstles to choose from. No massive changes from the franchise foundation to worry about, so older players of the series will get a feel for it straight-away. New players will pick up the idea quickly too, although may not want to fight with the controller issues if they come across them.

So far what I have learned playing Strike Vector is to expect the controls to actively resist your inputs and to respond in odd and seemingly arbitrary ways.  In one movement mode your aircraft will decide on its own when it would like to roll, whereas in the other movement mode you can no longer yaw or strafe up/down with VTOL controls.  Sometimes there is a cooldown between when you can switch these modes- but not always.  If you enter a boost in one mode you'll get a boost, but if you enter in the other mode nothing will happen.  Your mouse inputs and facing increase to high deltas between your vehicle heading and actual mouse direction, making firing projectiles and controlling your true heading messy and counter intuitive.
The array of weapons is interesting, and the customization options are very cool.  The art is great, the game looks really nice, and the sound design is also good.  I would recommend this game, if the controls weren't such a frustrating and dissappointing mess.

Do you like going fast?

Yes?
Get this game. It's beautiful with its UE4 graphics and attention to detail. Customization's great too.
Some issues are that when this game lags, it LAGS. Just a warning to bros with spotty connections.
Another issue is the learning curve this game has. For a while when you start out in this game you may feel like you are hopelessly outmatched as people fly circles around you. My advice is to keep trying! The moment it "clicks", you will find yourself actually getting kills, actually dodging missiles and terrain, and most importantly, having fun.
And that's what video games are all about.

Cliff-like learning curve, but does an incredible job of conveying a sense of going fast. Extremely unique gameplay. Looks great for having such a small team. A truly three-dimensional game with incredible freedom of movement and speed.
If you're reading the negative reviews, a lot of what they say about gameplay is wrong once you've played for a few hours.
The main key to this game is figuring out out that you can corner instantly by switching into harrier mode, turning towards where you want to go, and switching back into jet mode. You can do a 180 and be going the same speed in the opposite direction in about a second once you have it down. In most situations there's no reason to not be boosting when in jet mode. In addition, if you're about to hit a wall, you can switch into harrier mode to avoid death, unless you were extremely close. Hitting walls in jet mode will usually kill you instantly; hitting walls in harrier mode does no damage.
The second key is being able to fly at breakneck speed through small spaces in jet mode without killing yourself. That seems incredibly difficult at first, but it's something you'll get used to. It's not as hard as it seems.
Homing weapons are situationally useful, but due to how missile dodging works, using homing missiles to fight a veteran who's paying attention to you is pretty much the same as being unarmed. Everyone is going real fast and your weapons don't lock on, but the hitboxes are surprisingly permissive, and if you really still can't hit anything there's a hitscan shotgun. It's more difficult than other shooters. You'll just have to get better.
You'll spend at least your first two hours of so flying into walls, but it's an amazing game.

Lucy -The Eternity She Wished For -
is one hell of a Visual Novel. I was actually really hyped back when I first heard of this Visual novel through it's kickstarter, but since then almost forgot about it, which is why it's release on Steam took me by surprise. I knew that I would love this Visual Novel even back then as Chobits has been one of my favorite mangas for a long time now and one can easily draw a line between those two and the lesson they both tried to convey: 'What is it, that differenciates a human from an Android??'
I plowed through the entirety of this VN in two sittings, both clocking in at roughly 3 hours each, making this Visual novel not exceptionally long, but definitely not short in any way. It has to be noted that I did NOT go through every choice to see what changes, mainly because the story I got was too beautifully told to alter it in any way.
Speaking of the story, remember how I talked about Chobits a second ago?? I did not make the comparision lightly as it doesn't take a scientist (heh.) to see the similarities. Androids have become a part of everyday life for most people, safe for some who despise them. Our main character (who hates robots aswell, so there's a difference I guess) finds an Android at the junkyard and, spontaniously, decides to take her/it home. After a bit of time he finds himself strangely attracted to his new companion and consults his Robot-fanatic of a friend regarding robots (yes, I AM struggling with whether I should use Android or Robot, thanks for noticing) and their emotions, upon which said friend tells him that no matter how genuine their emotions might seem, they're fake and that he should under no circumstances fall in love with one. His guidance however is in vain as Mr. Main Character falls in love with her/it in no time flat.
What follows is a heartwrenching and -warming (please don't kill me for that one) love-story.
When the credits innitially rolled, I feared that it was over. That I had screwed up somewhere along the way. That a choice I made was a terrible one. Then the post-credits scene came, and I no longer knew what to do with myself as it seemed like there really WAS no better option... then I noticed that something was off about the main menu. That the 'Start' button was acting up. When I pressed it out of pure curiosity and hope, I found myself in a SECOND post-credits scene and boy... O boy, that was one plot-twist. I won't go into any specifics here, so all I will say is: I didn't even REMOTELY expect that plot-twist, holy Cthulhu.
So... I guess I can talk about some of the technicalities ('s that a word?? Well, it is now.) for a second.
There're voice options for Korean and Japanese, which I - as should be obvious - turned to Japanese in the blink of an eye.
However, there's only one character in the entire game that has voice-acting: Lucy Valentine herself. And jesus, that's some damn good voice-acting. All the emotions are translated exceptionally well and the character really comes to life via her voice (and isn't THAT an interesting statement??).
The art is pretty decent with the CG's being flatout beautiful.
There's no E-mote technology at work, but I never expected that anyways, so it's not really an interesting point.
Soo... should you buy it?? yes. Yes. YES, you should. There was not a single character at the end I could hate (no, not even the father... read the 'reunion' extra. ;-;), the story was simply beautiful and it`s only 10 bucks!

So I have been playing a lot of mafia-type games for the past year (Town of Salem, Throne of Lies, Mindnight, Camp Cadaver), and no matter how much I try to branch out, I always seem to return to ToL
Now, before we continue with this review, I will admit that I've ditched this game for weeks on end more than once. Does that mean that I hate it and that secretly I am a masochist? Could be- but the honest answer would be no- I do not hate this game.
Onto the actual review- the reason why I keep on returning to this game is because it's complex, it's beautiful, and it exposes all of humanity's good and bad traits. From truly careful and masterful ploys to earn your trust, to the most bitter and angry of words- Throne of Lies has it all. You're gonna all say "This is true for all social deduction games- what makes this one different?" Well, frankly, it's the sheer amount of classes, abilities, factions. This is the only game that I know of, that allows conversions (forcing people to join your faction), which can easily make a winning faction loose in a single night.
On another note that still relates to why I love this game is the developers and moderators- seldom have I seen devs so dedicated to listening (or reading as it were) to player feedback, and being extremely fast to respond to people's issues. If you report a player for a misdemeanor of some effect, you can rest assured that the mods will DEFINITELY take action.
Now, onto the not so pleasant things- the community can be incredibly toxic- to the point where you rage-quit and uninstall the game, only to re-install it again the next day.
Another issue is the fact that due to constant player demands, you will discover that a lot of classes suffer from endless changes, to the point of being removed (priest, soulcatcher and noble come to mind), which means that if you stay away from the game for two weeks, you might end up in a scenario where you do not know what's happening around you, because all of your abilities are changed to the core.
A final gripe that does not personally affect me, but non-the-less IS important, is that the game is NOT friendly to new players. There are too many mechanics to learn, too many classes and factions to figure our, and no real way to seperate new players from the experienced ones. While there is supposed to be a way to prevent new players from recieving certain roles (like King, Prince, or participation in Cult games), this often seems to not be the case, as I've seen on multiple occasions first-time players get King (which can be part of 3 different factions, thus make the way to achieve victory very different), which not only guarantees loss for them, but also all players that are part of their faction.
TL,DR: The game is awesome- graphics are entertaining, the sheer amount of classes will ensure that you'll always have something new to see or learn, and it's one of the most complicated social deduction games (I love that) that I've ever played. The developers truly love their playerbase, and they will always listen to your issues. With that being said, be sure to come prepared with your thickest skin and absolute disregard for people's opinions, otherwise this game will eat you and spit you out severely damaged. Also, if you're overall new to the "social deduction games" genre, be sure to watch a few videos, read up the basics on the Wiki a bit before starting up your first game- no one is gonna hold your hand while you learn the ropes.
Good luck and I hope to meet you in the throne room that is full of liars!
P.S.: English is NOT my native language- feel free to mock me for any grammar mistakes that you encounter!

A few friends asked me if they should get this game, so I'm writing a review to help anyone out.
Things to note:
- I have had this game less than a week but I have played ~20 hours
- I might have like a thousand hours in Town of Salem, so I just like this type of game
Pros:
+ in a game where other players directly impact your experience, the community takes this game seriously and works very hard.
( +/- unlike in town of salem, this means that most people don't play "characters" and instead focus on serious dialogues)
+ you can play it while doing something else (like, i read something during the downtime) or you can focus on it
+ the game is very balanced so you don't have to worry about a certain faction always winning
+ you can play an active role even when dead (by gaining gold for predicting who will be executed or killed at night)
+ each new game is challenging and different from the one before

Cons:
- the community can have a toxic view of the norm of a game. logs play too important of a role
- sometimes you can get the same class multiple times and that can get annoying
- there's a bit of a steep learning curve at first, with so many new roles.

( + they're more interesting than town of salem and are easy to get used to. plus, there are nice animations)
- the lobbies can be filled with people you've played games with before. community is not very large.
- music can get a little stale after a while

tl;dr: Game is lots of fun, strongest points being rewarding exploration, awesome combat and customization. It can feel clunky in certain areas, mostly due to the fact that it's a console port.
Pros:
+ Combat probably the game's strongest point, fantastic feeling. Tactical and strategical, most monsters have their very specific weak points or mechanics, and you need to know and adapt to all of them. I would summarize it as Dark souls lite.
+ Fair amount of specializations to choose from and customize in (Warrior, Ranger, Mage etc.)
+ Fairly numerous character creation options.
+ Abilities and actions all feel very impactful and real due to nice sound effects, Particularly as Ranger and Barbarian. Your arrow-hits knock people off their feet and your Two-hander Swings rip skeletons apart all with the right accomodating sound.
+ Simple story line. can be marked as con, but some people just want to smash monsters, so to me, it belongs in both.
+ Progression of Weapon and Armor visuals feels very rewarding, the difference from your first rusty long sword to the later stages is very stark.
+ Mods can upgrade the game a fair amount, particularly visually.
+ Companion System hits a nice balance between feeling impactful in which companion class you choose and not needing too much micro management, freeing you up to enjoy your own combat that much more. Though they could stand to keep their mouths shut a little more.
cons:
-Lack of multiple saves. This is by far my biggest complaint. Yes, you are able to train one character in every single specialization and play it out to the max, but you are not able to play multiple characters, since you only have one save at your disposal. This is clearly due to the game being ported from console, yet i find it somewhat irritating that something so important would be overlooked.
- Story is meager, and feels patchy in some areas. You just got done doing one thing and suddenly you have to do another for no apparent reason, which can be confusing and somewhat immersion-breaking.
- Voice acting is often criticized for being terrible. I did not perceive it as such. It's no master piece, but it's not completely unbearable either. What i will point out is that some voice actors were used multiple times and have a notable lack of enthusiasm in their voice.
- Melee Specializations can feels clunky due to cast times and position-lock-in mechanics, which is not exactly called for in a gameplay mechanic that by necessity asks for fluid controls and feel. to some degree, the mage classes suffer from this problem as well, though much less so.
- Some Quest markers are buggy, and a lack of location labels doesn't render the quest description very helpful either. You need to spend a few hours exploring and getting a feel for the world to be able to find those little outliers. They are rare, but can be annoying.
- That ♥♥♥♥ing lantern glow. Your lantern is a key item in the game, so you will be using it a lot, the lighting effect however is downright blinding. I recommend seeking out the mod which fixes this, as it makes it 10x more enjoyable to play.
- Companions are overeager to give you "tips", most notably some that you've heard over and over, which can be annoying.

"Pillars of Eternity" (developed by Obsidian Entertainment) is a very good "re-imagining" or "modernization" of the old Infinity Engine RPGs (role-playing games) from the late 1990s and early 2000s. It retains much of what made those older games enduring classics (expansive exploration, immersive story, tactical combat, etc.), but it is not a mere homage or re-tread; it also adds new elements of its own, such as an intuitive and user-friendly UI and very flexible character generation and progression systems. I would heartily recommend this not only to veterans and aficionados of the cRPGs (classic RPGs) of the past, but also to new players interested in entering the RPG genre for the first time!

Lucy -The Eternity She Wished For- developed by Modern Visual Arts Laboratory or "Mvizlab" in short and published by Modern Visual Arts Laboratory themselves they are an indie game development team made in Korea and is very new but to my surprise their first visual novel is surprisingly good I was not expecting this quality at all. In Lucy -The Eternity She Wished For- players are given choices to make in the game and depending on your choices it will change the outcome of the story. It features 2 or 3 endings? 1 of them being a Bad end and the other being a Good end. Relevant links will be can be found below.
Lucy ~The eternity she wished for~ is a Visual Novel, about a boy and an android. You play as the boy, who faces decisions and moral dilemmas that he struggles constantly in this near-future world.
In the near future, androids have become the way of the norm they can be found everywhere in human daily lives. Emotionless husks of metal have become a part of human society, much to the dismay of the boy because he had always preferred the "old methods". The robot he found at the dump site though, this one was different. It laughed, it cried, it smiled, just like a human… It has emotions..
Backgrounds are generally average nothing too fancy to talk about the background art, but as for the CGs I felt it is a little wasted not saying that it is bad in anyway but the CGs they tend to use glares to cover up the background which makes it bright which is good, but at the same time taking away the atmosphere that it could have been created with backgrounds to add more to the game as a whole. Something which caught my attention is that the UI or menu is very beautifully done I love the direction off the VN that it makes the menu and UI looks very realistic which contributes greatly to the overall atmosphere.
Nothing really stand out for the audio elements except for the fact that it cues in nicely and properly to fit in with the mood of the characters in turn manages to set the atmosphere perfectly every time. There is also voice acting for Lucy available both in Korean and Japanese voice.
To sum up will I recommend Lucy -The Eternity She Wished For- ? Simple answer yes, it is well worth your time and money for sure and for people who likes a sad story or maybe Sci-Fi be sure to get this game.

Masterpiece. What other word can I use to describe it? This game makes us question what fundamentally makes us human, what makes us alive. We can reduce a human being to being a simple chunk of autonomus flesh if we wanted to. We can reduce everything down to particle physics. But sometimes, it's hard to believe such simple things can create something so complex such as emotions. If we were able to replicate emotions on a machine, then will it be a machine pretending to have emotions? Or a machine capable of having emotions? To believe that machines are capable of having emotions is like denying that humans are a special existence.
Lucy -The Eternity She Wished For- is a very well made visual novel. The art is pretty. (The sprites show a range of emotions to represent what they are feeling.) The music is very good and the Japanese voice acting is also amazing.
If anyone has ever watched an anime called Chobits, I think you will find some similarities between the two.
If you like visual novels, anime etc, you would most likely love this. And when you play this game, expect an emotional ride.

One of my favorite ideas from the game is the thought that humanity doesn't like robots because they show the flaws of man.
Maybe I'm reading into too much into it or I'm just plain wrong. The point I'm trying to make is that this VN tries to make you think and tries to be more than just a story about a boy and his robot. That reason alone should be enough to at least give it a shot.

This game was my first experience with the survival genre, and after researching other games like DayZ I decided to purchase this one during a steam sale at half off, but now that i've played it a decent ammount - I would have felt OK had i purchased it at full price because it's a great game.
What's to like:
-Rich and detailed open world post apocalypse - close enough to present day to be believable, very pretty game.
-Dynamic gameplay - you are never sure how others will act and this can present some interesting scenarios
-Well balanced loot system - it's hard to find gear which makes it that much more rewarding to get good stuff (and will make you more paranoid to lose it when you've built up a good stash) - this gives the game an urgency for survival.
-Combat is an ends to a means and not the only goal - ammo and guns are limited so you have to decide if the random player you see looting a house is worth the battle when you might need that precious ammo to save yourself later.
What can be improved:
-Some small bugs/glitches here and there - but I've heard the dev team is very responsive to this and the game is still in alpha, i've never gotten to the point where these have detracted from the game in any meaningful way.
-more mutants would be nice as a way to get people to work closer together
Overall summary:
If you like to be tested in navigating an open world where danger could lurk in any corner then buy this game. Some of the best gaming experiences I've had where in this game - which is saying alot. The rush of hiding in a pitch black house with only a hatchet to defend yourself, while hoping the 3 guys with guns hunting you down wont find you is hard to match. The night/day cycle in this game is great - you can only see in dark houses with your falshlight - but doing so also gives your position away to others outside - this adds a great danger element to an aspect of the game that could easily turn into a grind without it.
Each "life" in this game will teach you something in how to survive - don't get discouraged too easily and you will enjoy many hours with this game. Buy it - you'll be glad you did.
(disclaimer - if you are looking for a COD style experience with cluttered HUD's and lots of shooting - go play another game, the HUD is minimal and aiming guns only works with iron sights which is a great aspect of this game.)

This is one of the very few open world survival games that's actually worth your time and money.
The gameplay dynamic is interesting, as it allows the player to choose when to take risks. Most other survival games play like a race or a time trial: "You must kill and eat a bear every 3 minutes to survive, or you will starve to death. Ready, get set, GO!" Thankfully, Stranded Deep is not that frantic, and is actually more realistic. Because you're on small islands, and sharks are the main enemy, you're not facing a serious risk until you try to leave your starting island. You can sit on your island, cook crabs, climb trees for coconuts, and build tools for basically as long as you need to. The pace is slower and the player is allowed more time to build their power, because there aren't monsters around every corner waiting to kill you 3 minutes after the game starts.
However, that does not mean the game is easy. Eventually, you will need to leave your island. You'll run out of wood to burn, or you'll run out of water, or something. Once you decide to leave, that's where the game gets challenging. You see, as soon as you venture into deep water, you'll run into the main enemy: sharks. They're in total control in the water, and it's easy for them to flip your raft, leave you bleeding, or worse. This creates the interesting dynamic I mentioned earlier; the player can choose when to take risks, by choosing when to enter deep water. This creates a system where the islands are safe havens, filled with food and resources, and the player can either choose to make the game difficult by advancing quickly, or easy by advancing slowly, consolidating your skills, banking food and water, and playing it safe (which is actually surprisingly similar to how real, deliberate survival attempts turn out).
As I mentioned, Stranded Deep is about long-term survival, not short and frantic races. Stranded Deep rewards common sense and critical thinking skills. Many items can be interacted with in realistic ways... You don't need a +10 Mithril Crafting Hammer to break rocks. You just need a small rock and a big rock, and a brain. The game rewards observation, and rewards players who behave realistically. It punishes players who behave recklessly. This can make the game slow at times, but overall it lends a sense of believability, and makes it more meaningful when you finally find an island worthy of use as a home base.
Additionally, many games also cherry-pick their screens, capturing the very few spots in the game that actually look good to provide a false representation of the graphics to potential buyers. Stranded Deep is much more honest; it actually looks as good as the screens. And, as a bonus, it's well optimized! It'll actually run maxed out on lower end hardware at playable framerates, like a GTX 750 and Pentium G3258, or thereabouts. Many other Early Access games look far worse than this and require top-tier hardware, which is just silly.
Overall, Stranded Deep is much more realistic and also more fun than other survival games. It has more natural pacing, and a more compelling risk/reward dynamic, and it's well optimized.

On its own it's a good game. The community wonders why its consistent playerbase is small and there's two reasons, both of which are common to online multiplayer games:
If you can ignore those negative aspects of this game, which, again, exist in pretty much all online PvP/multiplayer games, then this game is one of the greats if you ask me.
I like how every build option is unlocked right from the start, and you're free to experiment with various combinations of weapons, attachments and abilities. Everything after that is personal skills and cosmetics, which you earn after matches.
However, it should be noted that friendly fire seems to always be on, and some weapons are particularly tricky and unforgiving with it. Homing missiles for example can and will lock on to teammates, and they will pick your teammates as valid targets if your original target was shot down while it's already in flight.
The netcode is good and the game is playable even with 400+ ping, I find that it's extremely annoying to play with that much ping because while the enemies don't seem to rubberband, the terrain
and I've found myself getting stuck
a floating object as it bounced around and over me due to my ping to a European server (I'm from South East Asia).

Throne of Lies is a Mafia-style game. There are the usual Good, Evil, and Neutral classes; each with their own objectives and abilities.
In terms of gameplay, the game is good. There is a large amount of replay value with over 30+ classes and 2 different Evil factions. The King class guides players as the central authority. And most Good classes can be converted by special Evil classes into Evil classes. Hence, attention to detail is required to win as the Good faction.
In terms of story, there is practically none.
In terms of graphics, the game is... lacking. The UI is not very beautiful and the player models and animations are sloppy and unrefined.
In terms of music, the game is good. Most classes have unqiue sound bites and the general score is pleasent to listen to.
In terms of networking, the game is variable. Since the game is preer to peer, connectivity depends on the host.

Well, this is my Commentary on the whole product. The whole product is more, then just the gameplay, but i will start with the gameplay. I have to say, that the gameplay is really good. Everyone, who did no-kills runs in the previous games, can do so in this one. You can do open, deadly runs; silent, deadly runs and no-kill, silent runs. The game acknowledges this three style and i find the game to be a bit easier on no-kill, silent runs. If you like Splinter Cell, than this is a good game to play, whoever there is one big problem:
Every 30min the game crashes for no reason. It is a popular problem and i tried many of the popular solitions, but they did not work. So you have only 30min until the game crashes. This is a bit forgiving in campaign missions, because you have a lot of checkpoints, but it makes the extra mission increadible frustrating or impossible. Theses mission do not have permant checkpoints. If the game crashes the whole progress is lost and the multiplayer becomes inaccessible, if you ever get a connection to Ubisoft servers. The game came out in august 2013 and this bug is not yet fixed and there is no garanteed way to know if you will be affected. This is unexcusable.
My second problem comes with "Shadownet" or Ubisofts fancy way to make a central server unavoidable. Do you remember, how you could or could not connect to specific games-server back then? If you could not connect to a specific server, you choose another server and the problem was gone. You can't do this with Shadownet. If you can't connect to Shadownet, you can't play the multiplayer, because dedicated servers are the devil.
It is easy to understand, that i can not recommend a game, where the multiplayer does not work as good as from games from over 10 years ago (settlers 2, diablo 2, counterstrik 1.6) and you have a high chance to be plagued by a crash bug.
and it is best, if you got this 5-6€ for free. Play Dota2, CSGO, etc and get drops in form of items or cards. Sell this drops and buy SplinterCell with the drop money. This is probably the best way to enjoy this game.
This is sad, because the gameplay is good, but i can not support ♥♥♥♥♥♥, lazy and idle developers and publishers with a general recommendation.

The Good:
Given the age of the game I think the graphics hold up very well both on a technical level and an artistic level. The atmosphere is also somewhat unique consisting of a 1939 steampunk distopian world. The weapons all feel unique and provide different tactical arrangements given the situation your in. The 'gimmick' in this game is that you can slow, stop, and reverse time not only to defeat your enemies but also to solve puzzles. The game is also the right length, not too long for its own good but not short either. It knows exactly when its time is up.
I also thought the level design was excellent and varied, although most of the levels revolve around the standard FPS gameplay their were other levels consisitng of driving and turret levels to keep things fresh.
The Bad:
The story is a bit hard to follow at first and its hard to care about any of the characters in the game.
The game can also be a bit frustrating especially towards the end of the game.
The game is also very rushed near the end leading to a very anticlimatic battle.
Conclusion:
This game really surprised me, and highly underatted. The level design and areas reminded me a lot of half life 2 although no where near the same quality and that is the biggest problem with the game. For all its trying to do, other games have done it better making this game feel a bit average. Still I highly recommend you check this game out.

The first is the painfully cliche and predictitable storyline, you know - just stop the terrorists. A lot of them are pure daylight african terrorists encampments in the desert. Still, they are better than those in Double Agent. Dynasty Warriors 8: Xtreme Legends is a very satisfying game.  I just finished playing through each of the story modes (Only getting the historic endings so far.)  This game has a lot of features that will take hours to complete.  However, if you do not like hack and slash battlefield games this one might not be for you.  I would suggest trying out a Dynasty Warriors game on the Playstation 2 or PSP which are commonly avalable to see if you like this style of game.  It is WAY better than those ones though.
The number of weapon options is mind blowing and they are not clones of each other either they all handle differently.  Any character can play as any character too.  So if you like a character's weapon fighting style you can equip that weapon and essentially become that character.  Granted there is some disadvantages to it IE special attacks being abscent and such.
There is a pretty length free mode pretty much allowing you to play any stage with anyone.  There is also an ambition mode which I have not started yet but you select a character and play as a lowly soldier and work your way up.  Seems like a cool concept.
Would I suggest buying it full price?  Actually, yes I would because the number of hours you will get out of this game is well worth it.  Someone could easily spend 30+ hours on this game without seeing all the content.  So its like 2 dollars an hour at just casual play, not a bad price if you ask me.
Honestly, this is one of the better games I have played this year.  It held my attention and I could not wait to find out more and I also feel like I learned a little bit more about Chinese history (which I am entirely ignorant of in the first place.)
So if you want to run into a battlefield and slay countless souls this is the game for you.  Also it has some nice difficulty scaling too.

Lucy -The Eternity She Wished For- is definitely a Visual Novel worth experiencing.
Lucy -The Eternity She Wished For- is a thought provoking and emotional tale.
The art is lovely and gives the characters life in the story.
The music of the soundtrack is spot on,  both provoking and enhancing the experience.
Production values are high and quality immediately apparent.
A coming of age story for a young man almost completely at odds with his world and his relationship with Lucy, an android he came to know by chance.
Through his eyes we examine the role of technology in human society and effects upon that society.
Through his experiences, we question aspects of "nature vs. nurture" with regard to individual beliefs.
Within the experiences surrounding his fateful discovery, we question what it is that makes a human "real".
From his experiences, we question values, what is love and what it is to love.
One will smile, laugh, scowl, grimace and possibly cry during the course of the tale.
The overall atmosphere of the story has elements reminiscent of Planetarian and Narcissu, while the story touches issues in a manner that reminds me of scifi films A.I and Bicentennial Man.
The tales journey, as with life, is not always an easy one, but is worth the effort.
Recommended!

Though calling it “remastered” would be an exaggeration, this PC port was sorely needed. Capcom’s odd RPG is, after all, a rough gem.
Some of the game’s aspects feel strangely disconnected and the whole world (from lore to geography) seems rather shaky, and while the combat focuses on simpler mechanics the game still strives for an old-school vibe. Overall, a mixed bag. That said, for reasons I’m not entirely conscious of, the game just works. I’ve had some 100ish hours of gameplay up until now and can say that I look back with a great deal of affection.
To be sure, story-wise the game is a mess and graphically the it wasn’t state of the art even when it was released years ago (don’t get me started on the FPS drops on the PS3) – thematically, on the other hand, it all just seems to fit: some old JRPG vibes in a mythic European setting, a Monster Hunter-esque action roleplaying game with a party system and a more sinister background give it all a dreamy, surreal feel. I also think it safe to say the influences of Dark Souls (thematically) and Shadow Of The Colossus (mechanically) are felt throughout the game, mirroring at times the unspeakable horrors lurking in the depths of Lordran and the silent, solitary wilderness of the Forbidden Lands. And though it unabashedly copies features and themes from all over the place, it is a game entirely on its own.
Curious and unique, Dragon’s Dogma: Dark Arisen has given rise to a faithful cult of players and provided its niche with one of the most uneven (and yet heartfelt) experiences to date.

Dragon's Dogma is an engaging and epic title with fierce combat and works on PC very well. The story is fairly average as far as fantasy goes but the characters are believable and have a good level of depth and background (besides a few unexplained and somewhat bizarre scenes). As a huge fan of character customisation, this game really delivers - allowing you to customise not only your face and hair, but also your build and even to some extent your age - which all affects elements of the game. I really hope they make a sequel or at least another game set in the Dragon's Dogma universe.

Hardware engineers is quite a fun and addictive little game of managing your own little IT shop.
On one hand, you have to deal with customers that want to buy new hardware.
On the other hand, you have customers arriving with broken equipment, or their PC needs an upgrade.
Your challenge as the player is to properly balance customer care with IT repair work.
But it doesn't stop there... To build new equipment or to repair existing equipment, you have to get your hands dirty; you need to swap out hardware, drivers and programs all by yourself!
As someone who has repaired laptops and PCs myself since I was a teen, this game already comes pretty close to simulating and exposing the players to the decisions and problems of the IT store.
Someone in Green127 (if it's not a one-man company) has clearly used previous experience to shape the basics of this game.
To sum it all up, the developer has encased the game in simple, but charming graphics.
Even though Hardware Engineers is early release, it already has a good deal of gameplay and content. Updates also roll out fairly often with new content and fixes.

I’ve put more than twice as many hours into Dragon’s Dogma as I have Skyrim—and I kind of think that’s saying enough.
But I also think that Dragon’s Dogma deserves more. It is absolutely a unique game, and so I think it calls for a different kind of review.
I actually went hunting for Dragon’s Dogma. I knew what I wanted: a game with an NPC companion that was my own: one that I could create, one that had a personality of its own that I didn’t have to just pretend existed, one that had more than a handful of generic lines and didn’t break out into windy monologuing only when it progressed the story.
So the internet gave me Dragon’s Dogma. And Dragon’s Dogma gave me my pawn. He is my pawn: an NPC hand-crafted to behave the way I want him to, talk the way I want him to, and look the way I want him to. It’s kind of like having a self-groomed cat that actually listens to you and seems genuinely concerned about the traumatic events that your character must experience—and about as intelligent. And when you feel as though you have perfectly expressed yourself through your pawn, you may share him (or her) with the world and pray that he is as useful (and fashionably dressed) as you’d like to think he is. And then, of course join the fantastically supportive Steam community where you can marvel at, laugh at, and occasionally dismay over the AI antics of your shared pawns.
Of course Dragon’s Dogma offers more than just customizable NPCs. It has a somewhat interesting story, a mildly exciting world, and a memorable if not entirely likeable cast. And Troy Baker.
Combat, however, seems to be the main demographics’ draw. If you like the idea of crawling up a dragon’s knee so you can stab its heart while your pawn staggers it with arrows and your friend’s pawn tanks for you while your other friend’s pawn hangs back so she can conjure up the biggest, doom-ridden maelstrom spell she can, then you’d probably like this game. If you don’t like getting ganked by lowbie bandit mobs within the first 30 minutes of starting, then you may not like this game. And yes, there will be times when you run for your life, or die.
On the whole though, I highly recommend it. And if a mix of Dragon Age, the Sims, and a little bit of Pokemon woven into a Nihilistic setting of charmingly archaic dialogue and devoted NPCs that call you master sounds interesting to you, it is absolutely worth every penny and multiple playthroughs.

State of Decay is by far one of my all favourite zombie games.
It's centered around zombies and not like alot of other zombie games these days where you must also fight humans. The main story of SoD is decent but nothing amazing. Don't buy this game if you're only in it for the storyline. You'll only be left very dissapointed as there isn't much meat on the story. The gameplay on the other hand is what makes this game so addicting and entertaining.
The graphics are quite well and there is alot to explore. Ever wanted a zombie game with Sims elements? SoD is what you want. You and your community must survive and gather resources, with small events randomly being triggered around the community and game world. Each new community member that joins you is another someone you can play as. If your character dies you will reappear back at your base as one of your current members. The game itself is only in thirdperson, not that it's an issue, the characters are very detailed and interesting to play as and you almost never feel like playing the same one.
As for DLC, Breakdown offers alot of new content such as weapons and unlockable hero's, characters from the main storyline and a few bonuses. Breakdown also makes the game less storydriven and more focused on sandbox style. Surviving or doing whatever it is you wish. Breakdown also has a level stage system. This game is like putting Farcry 3 and The Sims together in a zombie infested world.  For those who haven't played either of those games, Farcry 3 had the notion of an open world with missions that string you along, but also with side missions that became repetitive later on.  The Sims was all about taking care of your people's needs and ultimately having them survive the real world.
In State of Decay, you have an open world that you can explore at your leisure, but with missions that string you along a primary path and secondary missions to enhance gameplay, but also become repetitive.  The latter half is all about maintain your home base and securing survivors within your base, and then to maintain their basic needs and emotional outbursts while trying to survive zombie onslaughts.
The game is very interesting and simulated.  You don't get big guns and gold from killing zombies, in fact, it's probably best to avoid zombies in most situations, because you gain nothing beyond some skill improvement, but also risk your character for permanent death!  That's right, if you die, it's permanent for that character (as far as I've witnessed thus far), but you can swap between any survivor character in your base once you friended them.  This is nice to break from boredom using just 1 character all the time, and everyone has their own strengths.  Also, other real life simulated aspects come into play, like noise attracting zombies, tension between characters, basic human needs, running out of breath when tired, etc.
Great game for a zombie simulation; however, I feel like a lot of it will become repetitive after so many hours of play, just like most open world sandboxes (except Skyrim! lol).

It’s been a while since I’ve played Sonic CD, so details may be fuzzy. However, Sonic CD is the first 2D Sonic game I played as an adult, which more or less means that it’s the first 2D Sonic game I really enjoyed. As a kid, I was told by advertisements and everything that Sonic’s fast. If you weren’t running at top speed for the whole stage, you’re playing it incorrectly. So I would get frustrated at 2D Sonic games when I couldn’t go fast…which, well, is pretty often if you aren’t a speedrunner. Fastforward to the modern era: I just played Sonic CD out of nowhere and played it like a normal platformer…and it was really fun!
Sonic CD isn’t like normal 2D Sonic games. It has this curious mechanic where you can visit level in the Past, Present, and Future. Unfortunately, I can’t quite say too much on how this works, but that’s fine. You don’t need to take advantage of the weird signs that say “Past,” “Present,” and “Future” to enjoy the game. I just went through it and did whatever and still enjoyed myself. The levels and bosses are engaging enough to have some fun for a few hours. Though I suppose looking into how this game’s time travel mechanic works could be beneficial to playing the game if you so desire. I’ve seen 100% runs of this game where you need to change time specifically, then search around each level for a machine to destroy and, well, I probably wouldn’t describe that as a fun time unless you want the satisfaction.
I’d say Sonic CD has depth to its mechanics and level design, but you can ignore them and still have a good time romping through levels like I did if you want to. Of course, you probably won’t get too much time out of the game and missing what makes it really interesting by doing my way, but I still think it was nice to experience regardless!

An absolute gem of a game and I kind of feel bad buying this game on sale. This is by far one of the best FPS games I have played. The time manipulation mechanic expands on what F.E.A.R. called "reflex time" and allows you to pause or reverse time in addition to being able slowing it down. Switching between the different modes allows for varied and gratuitous ways of dispatching your enemies. Level design is pretty good and the enemy AI is quite challenging. They will try to flank you or flush you out with grenades (or both!). They will even camp above a manhole and wait for you to come out and blow you to bits. There is plenty of CQB inside buildings and even a bit of trenches. There are also a few puzzles which will require you to make use of your timeshifting abilities to get through. The story is a bit sub-par and horribly confusing but then again, who cares about the story when you can pause time, pump a grunt full of holes with your scattergun, chuck a grenade, unpause time and then watch the guy explode in a glorious mix of blood, guts, and buckshot.
If you liked F.E.A.R. or Singularity then get this game too. You will not be disappointed.

But what it really made me do, is think.
We live our lives, matter/energy, moving in space-time. We are largely at the mercy of matter, energy, and space. Oh, there's gravity, sunlight, electromagnetism, electricity, hot, cold, etc.
But our concept of time is always the same: It's moving forward. Tick-tock-tick-tock.
None of us can really manipulate time. Make it run slower, or stop it, or even reverse it. Nope, that's not how we live our day-to-day lives.
But you know, if you can manipulate time like that, then seriously, we won't be at the mercy of matter, energy, and space so much. We can stop fire from burning, stop electricity from electrocuting, stop ourselves from plunging into water.
Suppose you are in a collapsing bridge. It falls, you along with it. Reverse time to the point that it is still standing. Heck, while time is in reverse, get the heck off that bridge. This game has enough scenarios like that.
Sh** if this game can make you re-think your concept of reality, then its a darn good game.

Saber Interactive creates an epic first person shooter that allows you to manipulate time in order to solve puzzles and defeat hordes of enemies. TimeShift accomplishes what other games only can dream off with brilliant mechanics and fantastic gameplay elements.
Timeshift offers a game that essentially has no elements of a story until the entire campaign is completed. Don’t worry once the game is over you will finally be given the story.
The campaign consists of twenty-four levels, each of varying length and difficulty. The campaign is a combination of puzzle solving, first person shooters, and boss fights. You have to use your suits to reverse time, pause time, and slow time in order to get through traps, operate systems, and defeat enemies. With a combination of boss fights and hordes of enemies you must accomplish objectives. Overall the campaign should take about eight hours, depending on difficulty. With the difficulty selection you can control the strength and numbers of the enemies, but the difficulty of the puzzles cannot be adjusted. The puzzles allow the campaign to be entertaining even if the campaign is on easy.
The game has nine weapons (KM-33, KM 2103 Karbine, Shattergun, Echo Rifle, ThunderBolt, E.M.F. Cannon, Bloodhound, Hell-Fire, and SurgeGun) and grenades. I found myself rarely using grenades throughout the campaign, because of the high weapon variability. Most of the guns have a secondary fire mode, which allows them to be versatile. Not only do you have a large variety of weapons to make the campaign entertaining, but you also have the ability to control time. The suit allows you to pause time, slow time, and reverse time. Each of these features can be used to change how the game plays. For example when enemies throw grenades you can reverse time in order to cause the grenades to go back to their host. You can pause time in order to heal yourself, and slow time to rush up to enemies and blast them before they can react. Time control combines elements of Max Paynes bullet time, and pushes it further with much more diversity.
TimeShift is a brilliant game that was ahead of tis time. The story is brilliant and complex, yet not clearly dictated. You will want to know what is going on, but after everything is over you will finally understand what happened. There are twenty-four levels and each level is of decent length. The gameplay offers both advanced concepts used in future titles, and also new concepts that although brilliant have never made an appearance again. With the ability to fully control time, either by outright stopping it, slowing it, and even reversing it creates a diverse game which combines all dimensions. TimeShift combines puzzle solving with action to create an epic adventure that is absolutely amazing. I would recommend TimeShift even if you pay full price, $19.99, it is still a good deal; although, if you can get TimeShift on sale it is a steal and I would completely recommend it.
Pros:
+Ability to stop, slow, and reverse time.
+Loads of weapons to mess around with that have secondary fire modes.
+Fast paced combat
+Puzzles that require you to use special tactics to solve.
+There are loads of ammo boxes so you don’t ever feel low on ammo.
+Epic boss fight that finishes the game in a bang.
+Loads of enemies that make the game refreshing.
Cons:
-The story doesn’t present itself till after you complete the entire campaign.
-Controls are not as obvious and it took me a while to figure out I could look down the barrel.
-Most of the weapons are not available till late in the game.

Forced is an interesting take on a co-op hack and slash. The foundation of the game  is sort of like Gauntlet, a  top down game where you pick a class and then mow down mobs and move through the battle areana.
But, fun as that is, that's not the point of the game. Each level has a puzzle or objective. So, imagine solving group puzzles and tossing balls back and forth, all while trying to survive wave after wave of fairly difficult enemies.

But the game itself, it took a little while to understand. After the first few games I wasn't sure how much enjoyment I'd get.  There are so many classes to learn their skills and the "rules" about identifying what the objective is each game and what classes are going to show up. After about 5 games I started to really understand and get interested and then everything just clicked. Suddenly I knew what was going on and the little quirks (like logkeeping, or fake logs), the lingo people use, the ways people can be deceitful. Then I was playing for 6 hours at a time because it became SO interesting!
I never thought I'd have so much fun dieing in a game and spectating to the end to see all the plot twists and turns that develop, some of my own doing that don't reveal themselves until days after my own death. This game's goal SHOULD be going fast. It would make sense for a Sonic game's goal to be going fast, and that is the goal of most sonic games. However, this game constantly stops momentum with crappily placed obstacles, and you are barely ever going fast. The game experience is ruined a ton of the time because it is easy to take more than .5 seconds to react. if it gave reaction time and didn't put walls and enemies in your path, it would be fun. Don't get me started on the stupidity of the time traveling. The time travel sounds fun, but don't be fooled. It is just a way to prevent you from having fun and is annoying. The mechanic is: you move fast enough for a period of time, and you time travel if you have touched a "Past" or "Future" signpost to obtain a "Past" or "Future" symbol respectively. The issue with this is as earlier stated, there are constantly obstacals thrown in your path. As such, the game has little boxes that push you back and forward at a constantly fast speed. These boxes are annoying, repetitive, and frusturating to find. This game would be better if it hadn't been made at the same time that sonic 2 was, because that team knew how to make a true sonic game.

It's a pretty solid FPS with some unique time shifting mechanics. Basically you have the ability to... as the name implies shift time. You can slow it down, stop it or reverse it, which could make for some interesting combat situations, but unfortunately that's not the case here, because mostly you'll just find yourself slowing down time in order to mow down groups of enemies with some ridiculously OP weapon, which is completely fine and I found enjoyable since you get to feel like greek god. There's a just a certain type of satisfaction to be had when your targets freak out and yell "THATS IMPOSSIBLE!" before getting blown apart into pieces by a timed explosive arrow. Where this game does put the full extent of your time shifting abilities to use is puzzle solving, I found the puzzles to be a little simple and repetitive but still interesting and clever, sometimes I'd stop to think how cool it was what I just did.
The story was mildly interesting, without spoiling too much you basically get sent back in time to take care of a renegade scientist who went back in time to take over the world, but due to how time travel works your time line doesn't get affected and you're actually just saving an alternate timeline... or something, I don't know, probably not but that's what I got from it. Time travel is complicated as ♥♥♥♥ so don't expect me to explain it ok? Anyway where this game TRULY shines is in it's art & graphics direction, it's got a really awesome mix between cyber and steampunk going on set in a nazi germany type aesthetic, it made me want to keep playing to see more of this world.
So in conclusion I wouldn't call this game underrated as steam tags suggest, its rather a more obscure title set in a cool♥♥♥♥♥world where you get to feel like a god. Definitely worth a playthrough if you enjoy FPS. I'd give this game about a 7/Bioshock.

TimeShift is a game about you being a nameless doctor guy in a badass-looking suit with the even more badass ability of time manipulation. Another doctor, an evil one, jumps into the Alpha Suit, a work-in-progress concept for a military suit or something, which someone had the idea of putting time-traveling stuff into. He goes back in time to 1930's or so and starts some kind of totalitarian rule using his, what I assume, knowledge to advance technology to create cool stuff like energy weapons and a giant mechanical spider patrolling town. You, the silent protagonist, jump into the Beta Suit, the better-in-every-way version 2 of the Quantum Suit project or whatever, and go after him. Story is nothing special, but I think it's enough to make you go forward.
You're armed with 3 weapons at a time, a few grenades and a melee attack. You also got the ability to slow down time, stop it completely and even reverse it. It's vital in combat and nothing says badass like stopping time, grabbing an enemy's gun, emptying the clip in his face, and then resume time and watching him fly. In fact, for some enemies, that's required.
It's incredibly fun in the beginning, but but about halfway through the game it's just nothing special anymore.
Then you have the puzzles, which are nothing special and don't feel rewarding, but they aren't hard either. They just stop your for a second or two and when they're solved you just move on.
Graphics are meh, sound is meh, animations are meh. For me, the best thing is the art design. Some of the things you see in the game look downright awesome.
Conclusion: Get it on sale and play it when you're bored.

Very disappoint after seeing all the praise the game gets for being underrated. Pitiful story, worse gunplay, and gimmicky timeshift mechanics.
First of all, there is no sprint, which wouldn't be a problem but the main character casually walks in the most life threatening situations. You can often die trying to walk to cover when your time powers run out. It tried to make you think about where you should be as you run out of powers but it's more like putting anvils on your shoes and calling it a design choice.
The time powers were also a very big disappoint. Neat concepts but the execution was very poor. The time rewind and time stop use so much power it seems they were only put in to solve the extremely simple time "puzzles"; such as walking over the millions of electrified puddles. Time slow is about 90% of power usage as it's the only power that gives you any real chance in combat vs more than one soldier.
Now the gunplay isn't the worse I've seen in a game, but the way enemies can soak up about half of a magazine til death makes even the best FPSer turn into a camper while his OP slow time power comes back. I was never a fan of the bullet sponge enemies because it makes combat more gimmicky and campy. Even if you are quicker than the enemy it doesn't matter when you have to go through half a mag to kill one enemy while 2 others are shooting. Combat tends to be either slaughter everyone while in time slow mode then camp to wait for power to come back, or spam grenades for one hit kills then pick up more from their bodies. The only time combat felt somewhat fair outside of time slow was either the ballistic crossbow or sniping headshots, and even then enemies all had pinpoint accuracy from a mile away; and mouse sensitivity is iffy and ignores small movements when zoomed in too far in scope.
The game also doesn't understand what pacing or transitions are. The weapons go from the weakest assault rifle ever made, to the most overpowered weapons. The game goes from frustrating to super easy mode with the one shot crossbow, or infinite ammo boxes with a sniper or rocket launcher next to them. It still ends up being time slow then murder everyone; it just gets easier being able to one shot everyone before they murder you with pinpoint accuracy from a mile away when your time slow runs our and you are out of cover.
I mean, for an old game it isn't as bad as what I've seen, but it definitely doesn't deserve all the praise  when it really is just semi-unique and but a very gimmicky one trick pony

Shellshock Live is that classic 2D tank game you probably know of…but with online Multiplayer and a crazy weapon selection that surpasses even Worms. For the most part, the gameplay is turn-based where you move your tank a small distance each turn, then put an angle and set power into your shot, then hope you calculated it right and it hits the enemy. The huge weapon variety prevents it from being stale, though, as you may have to plan different strategies depending on what weapons the crates give you. There’s not much to describe, but I assure you it’s fun and easy to get into, especially with friends.
There are a few flaws, though. The biggest flaw is the upgrading system. As you play more, you can upgrade your tank’s health, movement, etc. This can create unfair discrepancies between you and friends if one decides to play alone or if someone’s new. You pretty much have to reset tanks at that point. Also, you unlock weapons and the player with the wider weapon pool is usually at an advantage. The game has a few ways to try and balance this, but I think it would’ve been more fun and easier to pick up with anyone if everyone had the same tank stats and all weapons unlocked.
Otherwise, I think this game is definitely worth a shot. If you can get your friends in on it, I think that’s definitely the route to go…as long as you all stay leveled near each other.

Out of the many games that try to 'simulate' a zombie survival setting up to this day, State of Decay is probably as close to home as it can get.. unless you really do have a 'military' background and all you seek from a zombie apocalypse is to either be a hero in a one-man army or make life a living hell for everyone else.
The game plays best with a controller and I would strongly discourage anyone from playing it with the keyboard and mouse as the controls and interface may take away a chunk of the enjoyment. Combat feels satisfyingly meaty and comes with it's own risks both in melee and ranged as one could imagine. The game also has you choosing and setting up your own safe home and reinforcing it by scavenging for supplies and/or survivors to help out in defending it. Management of resources and community relations is present though it may not be as complex or custom as some people desire it to be. But for that matter, I would have to wonder if that's not asking too much. Other than that, it's an open world that's susceptible to your own interpretation and leisure.
I've heard and read that the game does get repetitive eventually but in all honesty, which game doesn't suffer from this problem without either a captivating storyline or mechanic which are both subject to personal opinion. Some of these concerns are also easily solved with the inclusion of the 'Breakdown DLC' though it does come with an additional pricetag.
In short.. it's hard to get exactly everything you want out of a game but for what it's worth, I think this game offers more than enough for the zombie survival fanatic that is more into the actual aspect of surviving instead of the PvP environment / bandit-lifestyle a zombie apocalypse would entail.

Hypothetical situation you're a gladiator and spirits are always with you because you have a spirit mentor he's called Belfry or something. He has a mental disorder, so he's got multiple personalities and one of them is a capital arsehat. that's why you have to be a gladiator.
Once they establish the plot, you get to punch a scarecrow with a weapon and then you get to punch it REALLY hard and then you're a real gladiator. This is a good game to play with a controller. After you're a real gladiator, you have to go fight real enemies, and then you're a true gladiator. Once you do that, you can start playing actual levels, and then you can be acknowledged as a gladiator.
Levels are fun with friends, if you happen to have any. Friends are useful because they do everything wrong and will inevitably make the game harder. So don't try to play this with friends, they're usually really bad at this. If you do play with friends out of the kindness of your heart, it is not required that you acknowledge them as gladiators. You may opt to refer to them as peasent, commoner, or perhaps dead.
Fighting is fun because you pick a weapon and then you kill enemies with it. When you kill an enemy a few times, it loses health and gains marks instead. Marks are sort of like a currency in this game, where enemies can trade you their health points for more marks. Once they've made this trade, they can opt  to sell them to you in exchange for more damage. Through this method, you can kill enemies, and become a gladiator.
Becoming a gladiator is harder than just killing enemies though. you need to get crystals and stuff, and those let you get more abilities and passive things and active abilities and passive abilities, as well as skills which you acquire by collecting gems.
There is also a soundtrack in the game, although I do not remember any of it. It is probably gladiator music. I can not confirm this. I would give this game anywhere from 10 to 12 dollars, because I think it was on sale.
Now is a good time to buy it, since you can get it at full price again.
This is a definite must-have for anyone that thinks they might like to be a gladiator, in any sense of the word.

I've now spent a little over 100 hours playing this game and there are a few things to say about it that are positive:
- The graphics and the landscapes are sometimes beautiful and render efficiently on even my somewhat aged machine
- Driving vehicles in the game is a very fun, though fleeting, experience
- There is definitely a rush of adrenaline when you're fully equipped and looting Hayward in the dark of the night. And it's quickly followed by desperation when a group of strangers sees you, anger when you are one-shotted, and disbelief when you convince yourself you can run back to your death spot before the 15 min despawn period has elapsed.
But there are a lot of bad things about this game as well:
- There's not really anything to do in the game. Sure, you can run around and loot. And fix cars. And kill people. But that gets really boring, and the lack of any real objective just leads people to roam around in groups and kill you for no real reason, even if you are obviously sans weapons.
- The introduction of the female character has been a disaster. While I'm sure the developer meant well, the introduction on Valentines Day (i.e. forced sexualization of females) coupled with the fact that the female char is nerfed (punches, kicks are weaker than male, jump height was decreased) make me question who is making decisions at the company.
- Lack diversity. If the developer is interested in being inclusive, they would include additional races and a transgender option from the character setup. I'm not sure whose utopia a bunch of bald white males running around in army boots reflects, but it's disturbing to me.
- Mutants have very poor AI and are extremely easy to defeat.
- Few vehicles which require a lot of dedication to fix (average is probably over 1hr to find all components). Once fixed, their health will decline for running into things, but they can supposedly be repaired with a lug wrench. But it doesn't work, and even if you get the vehicle health back to 100% it will still explode for bumping into a sidewalk.
- That coughing noise: Sometimes there is a random coughing noise when you are running around in the woods and I don't like it or understand why it is in the game.
- The Voice of God: This should be self-explanatory, but when you ascend the skyway bridge to heaven you are greeted by what I assume is the voice of God. I don't know if this is some kind of joke, but I used an app to identify the speaker and, you guessed it, it's Pol Pot. Not funny.
Basically if the above points are addressed I will change my recommendation of this game.
Edit: Now that Playerunknown's battlegrounds has been released I guess the Miscreated developers can go ahead and begin filing for insolvency.

Timeshift is the prime example of a good concept (time manipulation) badly rendered. The story in itself is utterly slim and unattractive (and with quite the erratic narrative) :  a scientist, Krone, decied to found his own empire in an alternate timeline and you go after him. The end. No surprises, no twist, no incentive to continue.
The hero is a soulless mute, joining the Resistance just because and being ordered around, while nobody bats and eyelid at a suit guy appearing from nowhere and able to manipulate time around him.
There's a grand total of two timejumps !
But well, story is not meant to be the strongest point of a FPS. Problem is, the gameplay is also lacking. Not that it plays badly- on the opposite, it plays quite smoothly. But the game is far too easy. Your ability to slow time, combined with the quick regeneration of your health and a genous cooldown for time-controlling abilities, makes you near-invulnerable if you stay cautious. The game compensates by unleashing hordes of brainless soldiers, but it just makes the fights longer, not more interesting.
The puzzles are short of anything creative. A puddle of electrified water ? Stop the time, the water is solidified, go unscathed. The bridge is collapsing ? Activate return, walk on it as it goes back in time for your needs. It won't challenge your intellect, rest assured.
The weapons feel good, especially the explosive crossbow, but in the end you feel like you spend most of your times pushing buttons and going back. Cooke, the leader of the Resistance, yelling at you every twenty seconds in some sections till you accomplish the objective is quite unnerving.
The game is mercifully rather short- about 8 hours, without replay value. In a way, it's quite soothing because you stomp the ennemies with your arsenal and slow time capacity, but it was really clunky and uninspired at the time, it's not better now.
If you want a FPS with the Time them and a good dose of humor, try Time Splitters : Future Perfect. Else, even Singularity is more convincing than Timeshift : at least you interact with the world, you're not a mute puppet in a suit.
Surely Saber Interactive is doing better now, but then they have also produced Battle Los Angeles... Not the brightest past.

TimeShift starts out as your run-of-the-mill shooter, weapons handle nicely..but nothing notable, AI is fairly average, and the visuals were good for the time (but not great). The Time control mechanic works really nicely in this game, and that's when it evolves from run-of-the-mill to something special. It's a hidden gem, overlooked by the big boys of the time (Gears, CoD4, Halo 3 and so on).
-You Can SLOW DOWN AND PAUSE TIME (This alows you to pull off some really neat looking kills, and hell even steal your
opponet's weapon and shoot em' in the face)
-You Can REWIND/REVERSE TIME (Ever had a nade thrown in your face, or the enemy spotting you too quickly and ruining your fairly stealthy approach? No problem just reverse time and handle the situation!
People complain about the Time control mechanic being too short or too gimicky..but in reality with the help of a good shot lined up and time slowed you can easily take out 5-6 enemies within your short burst of Time halted/slowed.
Overall, a good game..It's not great, but it is something unique. Definitely worth taking a look at if you haven't already.

Story and Lore: Nice and sweet, not a whole lot here but the main questline helps pace the player if they want to be perfectly aligned with tier progression. The missions kind of serve as "final boss fights" for each tier if you will and the lore is a great side quest when you have nothing to do or if you are really into it as well as the numerous races that you meet on your journey. Plus the in game abc music is great!
Soundtrack: It's great ambience since there are very few times I actually notice it because I'm usually hearing the crunch of my bones from falling or gunshots but the few times I have sat back and appreciated it I have loved it. The Sound effects are nice too, really imersing me from being singed, music softened when underwater or even doors opening. Not overly impressive or noticeable but I'd argue that's perfect for the gameplay.
Gameplay: Combat and pretty simple with a diverse range of options from varying guns, weapons and wands. Crafting is fairly simple once you get used to the dozen or so different crafting tables. The mechanics for bosses are fun to learn and really give you a sense of satisfaction when you blitz through it with very little problems. End game however is where it kinda stumbles since you are really left to your own devices after you've already done everything, you can perfect your crew or furnish your ship or colonise a planet for your own devices or achievement/collection hunt.
